results.name: familiar_vs_plain_outlier_rule_contrast
results.description: In >=3-example sets where all but one example share a final digit or a parity, yes rate for non-example targets obeying that majority rule when the lone outlier is a familiar number (1, 100, power of 2, square, 27, multiple of 10) minus when it is unremarkable; observed below null means people do not excuse familiar outliers more than plain ones as strongly as the familiar-stray model predicts, above means they excuse them even more.

results.name: gcd_multiple_contrast
results.description: In >=2-example sets whose examples' gcd is >=3, yes rate for non-example targets that are multiples of the gcd minus yes rate for non-multiples (both excluding targets sharing a final digit with any example); observed above null means people generalise the multiples rule more sharply than the model predicts, below means less sharply.

# name: gcd_multiple_contrast
# description: In >=2-example sets whose examples' gcd is >=3, yes rate for non-example targets that are multiples of the gcd minus yes rate for non-multiples (both excluding targets sharing a final digit with any example); observed above null means people generalise the multiples rule more sharply than the model predicts, below means less sharply.

def _sets(df):
    """Per row: tuple of examples (shown order). Parsed once per unique set."""
    u = pd.unique(df["number_set"].astype(str))
    parsed = {s: tuple(int(x) for x in s.split(",")) for s in u}
    return df["number_set"].astype(str).map(parsed), parsed

def _rate(r, m):
    m = np.asarray(m, dtype=bool)
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

FAMILIAR = set([1, 100] + [2 ** k for k in range(1, 7)] + [k * k for k in range(2, 10)] + [27] + list(range(10, 100, 10)))

def test_statistic(df):
    ex, parsed = _sets(df)
    g = {s: (math.gcd(*e) if len(e) >= 2 else 0) for s, e in parsed.items()}
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    gg = df["number_set"].astype(str).map(g).to_numpy(int)
    clean = np.array([(tt not in e) and all(tt % 10 != x % 10 for x in e) for tt, e in zip(t, ex)])
    sel = (gg >= 3) & clean
    mult = t % np.maximum(gg, 1) == 0
    return _rate(r, sel & mult) - _rate(r, sel & ~mult)

results.name: familiar_vs_plain_example_target_contrast
results.description: Among trials whose target equals an example of a >=2-example set, yes rate when that example is a familiar number (1, 100, powers of 2, squares, 27, multiples of 10) minus when it is not; observed above null means people discount familiar-number examples as strays less than the familiar-stray model predicts, below means more.

def _sets(df):
    """Per row: tuple of examples (shown order). Parsed once per unique set."""
    u = pd.unique(df["number_set"].astype(str))
    parsed = {s: tuple(int(x) for x in s.split(",")) for s in u}
    return df["number_set"].astype(str).map(parsed), parsed

def _rate(r, m):
    m = np.asarray(m, dtype=bool)
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

FAMILIAR = set([1, 100] + [2 ** k for k in range(1, 7)] + [k * k for k in range(2, 10)] + [27] + list(range(10, 100, 10)))

def test_statistic(df):
    ex, _ = _sets(df)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    is_ex = np.array([(tt in e) and len(e) >= 2 for tt, e in zip(t, ex)])
    fam = np.array([tt in FAMILIAR for tt in t])
    return _rate(r, is_ex & fam) - _rate(r, is_ex & ~fam)

results.name: target_is_example_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate on trials whose target equals one of the set's examples; observed below null means people endorse shown examples less than the model (they write off more examples as strays), above means the model over-attributes examples to strays.

results.name: power_of_two_member_yes
results.description: In >=2-example sets whose examples are all powers of 2 (2..64) and not all members of a smaller powers-of-m rule (m=4,8), yes rate for non-example power-of-2 targets; observed above null means people favour the powers-of-2 rule more than the family-only prior (equal weight for all powers-of-m rules) allows, below means less.

results.name: tiny_power_rule_broad_member_yes
results.description: In >=2-example sets whose examples all lie in a tiny powers-of-m rule (m>=3, at most 4 members, e.g. {8,64}, {9,81}, {4,16,64}), yes rate for non-example targets that are powers of 2, powers of 3, squares or cubes but outside that tiny rule; observed above null means people generalise to the broader familiar rule more than the size principle with equal within-family priors predicts, below means less.

results.name: square_member_yes_in_square_sets
results.description: In >=2-example sets whose examples are all perfect squares (1..100) but not all in one powers-of-m rule, yes rate for non-example square targets; observed above null means people favour the squares rule more than the model's family-level prior predicts, below means less.

# name: square_member_yes_in_square_sets
# description: In >=2-example sets whose examples are all perfect squares (1..100) but not all in one powers-of-m rule, yes rate for non-example square targets; observed above null means people favour the squares rule more than the model's family-level prior predicts, below means less.

def _sets(df):
    """Per row: tuple of examples (shown order). Parsed once per unique set."""
    u = pd.unique(df["number_set"].astype(str))
    parsed = {s: tuple(int(x) for x in s.split(",")) for s in u}
    return df["number_set"].astype(str).map(parsed), parsed

def _rate(r, m):
    m = np.asarray(m, dtype=bool)
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

FAMILIAR = set([1, 100] + [2 ** k for k in range(1, 7)] + [k * k for k in range(2, 10)] + [27] + list(range(10, 100, 10)))

def test_statistic(df):
    ex, parsed = _sets(df)
    SQ = set(k * k for k in range(1, 11))
    tiny = [set(m ** k for k in range(1, 8) if m ** k <= 100) for m in range(2, 11)]
    ok = {s: len(e) >= 2 and all(x in SQ for x in e) and not any(all(x in T for x in e) for T in tiny) for s, e in parsed.items()}
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    sel = df["number_set"].astype(str).map(ok).to_numpy(bool)
    nonex = np.array([tt not in e for tt, e in zip(t, ex)])
    return _rate(r, sel & nonex & np.isin(t, list(SQ)))

results.name: even_parity_only_yes
results.description: In >=2-example sets whose examples are all even and do not all share a final digit, yes rate for non-example even targets that are NOT multiples of the examples' gcd (when gcd>2) -- i.e. supported only by the 'even' rule or ranges; observed above null means people use the parity rule more than the model predicts, below means less.
